title: Kansas City Didn't Leave Out Its African Entrepreneurs. It Didn't Know They Existed.
description:
What happens when a city's entrepreneurs aren't excluded from the economy, just invisible to it?

On this episode of The Disruption Lab, recorded live in front of a studio audience, host Kevin McGinnis sits down with Suzanne Gunn. She is a former oncology nurse, med spa owner, couture designer, founder of AfroKC, and co-founder of a planned Fashion and Beauty Innovation Campus in Kansas City. Every one of those ventures traces back to one person: her mother. She died of cancer after being misdiagnosed four times in Kenya, and her quiet, community-first way of living became the blueprint Suzanne didn't recognize until it was almost too late.

Today we talk about everything she's built since:

a med spa that safely treats oncology patients
a couture label shown at Kansas City Fashion Week
a retail line selling handmade goods from African artisans
AfroKC, a festival she started after realizing the region hadn't excluded African-owned businesses so much as never known they existed
a planned Fashion and Beauty Innovation Campus

Recorded live, Kevin McGinnis talks with Suzanne about grief, a near-breakdown, why balance is a myth, and what it takes to build the community infrastructure most founders take for granted.

title: Raising a Black Business in Kansas City
description:
Kansas City is a thriving hub for entrepreneurs, and at Keystone we continually witness the incredible potential of this vibrant city. With its abundance of creative individuals, Kansas City has become a fertile ground for startups and ideas. The city itself acts as an incubator, fostering an environment where innovation flourishes.



In a recent session, we explore the stories of entrepreneurs who are working to create safe and social spaces for the black community. Their journeys and hard work exemplify how this city's unique ecosystem can nurtures and supports the growth of black businesses, creating a powerful impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.



Kansas City stands as a testament to the power of diversity, ingenuity, and the boundless opportunities that await those who choose to raise their businesses within its thriving community.

title: Black Entrepreneurship Week: Empowering Black Entrepreneurs in Kansas City
description:
Immerse yourself in an enriching dialogue as Craig Moore converses with the visionary co-founders of Black Entrepreneurship Week in Kansas City, shedding light on the inception, execution, and forward-looking strategies of this seminal event. The thoughtful conversation extends a lens into the indomitable spirit of Black entrepreneurs and aims to amplify the vital conversations about fostering an inclusive, vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem in Kansas City.

Key Highlights Include:

The conceptualization and launch of Black Entrepreneurship Week.
The week’s events, designed to uplift and champion Black entrepreneurs.
Essential tools, strategies, and resources unveiled during the week.
Visionary goals for establishing a nurturing platform for Black entrepreneurs.
Future aspirations and plans to evolve and expand the event.
About Black Entrepreneurship Week:
Black Entrepreneurship Week is not merely an event; it's a movement set in motion to reshape the entrepreneurial landscape in Kansas City. Tailored to be a resource-rich platform, the week facilitates the cross-pollination of ideas, robust networking opportunities, and an avenue to access crucial resources, encapsulating a wholesome approach toward nurturing Black entrepreneurship.

Delve into the detailed, behind-the-scenes perspectives and insights from the co-founders, as they navigate through the challenges and triumphs of organizing a week dedicated to Black entrepreneurship. Understand their motivations, the impact of the initiative, and the lasting change they envisage for the future of entrepreneurship in the community.

Join Craig and the co-founders in this insightful discussion to explore the ways Black Entrepreneurship Week is shaping a more equitable, prosperous future for all.

For further updates and more details on Black Entrepreneurship Week, search "Black Entrepreneurship Week Kansas City" on your preferred search engine or visit the official website.
